intro: Acceleration is now measured, not theorized, while safety, power, and oversight lag behind.

pulse.text: Frontier development is now arguing over measured self-acceleration, with METR estimating 1.7x faster capabilities progress at Anthropic and staff inferring ~10x researcher uplift, paired with concrete deployment risks like SSH-agent forwarding and 284B-parameter models running on 64GB of CPU RAM. Public reaction remains anchored in electricity and bills, with 40 of 41 anti-data-center ballots passing and reporting from Data Center Alley tracing opposition to grid strain and behind-the-meter gas turbines. The research community is preoccupied with AI reshaping science itself, from an AI-assisted Lean-certified proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture to ICLR reviews flagged as AI-generated and early-career mathematicians reporting darker career outlooks.
pulse.reading: Measured 1.7x RSI speedup plus SSH-agent leak holds risk elevated.

items.title: Ajeya: AI is dramatically accelerating AI research right now
items.note: Anthropic disclosed it may imminently meet its RSP trigger for dramatically accelerated progress, defined as twice the fastest pre-AI rate and attributable to AI doing AI R&D. METR's deep-access work behind that claim points to ~1.7x faster overall capabilities progress, implying researcher-level uplift near 10-12x. That turns recursive self-improvement from a forecast into a number to argue about.
items.author: Zach Stein-Perlman

items.title: Where is all the AI safety research uplift?
items.note: Buck points out the awkward corollary: if capabilities researchers are getting ~10x from Mythos 5 and Opus 5.5, safety researchers with the same models should be too. The absence of a visible 10x in safety results is itself evidence about where the uplift goes. It reframes RSI as asymmetric by default, not neutral.
items.author: Buck

items.title: ChatGPT Desktop forwards your SSH agent to remote machines
items.note: ChatGPT Desktop forwards a local SSH agent to remote execution, so code running elsewhere can authenticate as you and push to private GitHub repos. The linked Codex thread provides proof-of-behavior, not just a policy worry. For agentic coding tools, credential boundaries are now the control problem.
items.author: DenGorbachev

items.title: The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity
items.note: Reporting from Ashburn argues the data-center revolt is less culture war than megawatts: typical facilities draw 54MW, frontier training sites want 300MW to 6,000MW, increasingly behind-the-meter on gas turbines. Voters approved 40 of 41 anti-data-center measures over bills, water, and diesel backup. Power procurement, not messaging, will set the pace of buildout.
items.author: James O'Donnell

items.title: Llama-modchip: 284B DeepSeek on 64GB RAM, no GPU
items.note: A set of llama.cpp patches and Fractal-64 quantization compresses DeepSeek-V4-Flash from 76.87 GiB to 56.56 GiB at 1.71 bits per weight, fitting 284B total parameters into 64GB RAM with 256K context. Reported throughput is 44 tok/s prefill on a 16-core Zen 5 with no GPU. Open frontier-class MoE no longer needs a cluster to run.
items.author: joshcsimmons

items.title: Fable 5.2 and Jagged AGI
items.note: Mollick tests Claude Fable 5.2 across video generation, reverse-engineering a USB keyboard into six playable games, drafting a fundable business from 201 municipal agendas, and reconstructing Auden's 1941 syllabus. He grades it as almost-AGI on computer-only expert work: brilliant first drafts, unreliable at running the business alone. The jaggedness has moved from hallucinations to follow-through.
items.author: Ethan Mollick

items.title: Aaronson-Ambainis Conjecture proved! (By AI, of course)
items.note: Physical Superintelligence reports a proof of the 2009 Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture with bound ~1/d^6, obtained with an internal Claude plus research harness and backed by a Lean certificate. Exposition by Blanc, Docter, Strassle and Tan is already circulating. It rules out superpolynomial quantum advantage for decision problems on random inputs, leaving Shor and physics simulation untouched.
items.author: Scott
